label: Higher Education
categoryDescription: Knectar partners with leading educational institutions to deliver digital solutions that empower learning, collaboration, and innovation. Knectar partners with leading educational institutions to deliver digital solutions that empower learning, collaboration, and innovation.

submenu.label: Carnegie Mellon University
submenu.projectTitle: Carnegie Mellon: One CMS for the flagship and the unit sites
submenu.project_haiku: Carnegie Mellon needed the flagship site and the department sites to share a design system without sharing a single editor. We built that distribution on Drupal, GitLab, and Pantheon, with CMU reviewing every merge.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need unit sites that can publish on their own and still look like the university? That is the system we built with Carnegie Mellon.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Carnegie Mellon and Carnegie Higher Ed set out to replace a web presence that had become hard to govern. Departments needed to publish on their own. The university needed one brand, one component set, and a path from a reviewed merge to production. The work ran about eighteen months.

What we built

Knectar implemented the Drupal distribution. Development sits in GitLab. Hosting is a Pantheon upstream. A feature is a merge request that CMU's own developers review before it reaches the pipeline. The flagship, cmu.edu, and the unit sites draw on the same components.

Outcomes

A department can run its site. A change to the system still passes through CMU's review before it is on the public web.

submenu.label: Clarkson University
submenu.projectTitle: Clarkson University: A Drupal 9 site on one domain
submenu.project_haiku: Clarkson hired Carnegie to rethink the university site and Knectar to build it. The result is Drupal 9 on Pantheon: one site, editors working in Paragraphs, and the old Drupal 8 content brought across.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a university site your editors can assemble, on a platform you can keep? We built that for Clarkson.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

In 2022 Clarkson University asked Carnegie, formerly mStoner, to reimagine the institutional site. Discovery called for the brand and the three campuses to read as one place, for WCAG 2.1 AA, and for faculty, events, and alerts to stop living on separate systems. Carnegie wrote the strategy and the technical blueprint. Knectar implemented it.

What we built

The site is Drupal 9 on Pantheon. Drupal 8 content and the scattered subdomains came into that one site. Editors build pages from Paragraphs: heroes, statistics, features, testimonials. The front end is the from-scratch code Carnegie specified, with PostCSS and webpack, so the university kept a style guide it can own. The blueprint also covered PeopleSoft for faculty, EMS for events, Rave Alert for emergencies, personalization through Clarity, and search through Funnelback.

Outcomes

Clarkson has one public site, a CMS distributed editors can use, and a front end the university can keep maintaining after the launch team is gone.

submenu.label: Yale Center for British Art
submenu.projectTitle: Yale Center for British Art: The museum site and the collection search
submenu.project_haiku: The Yale Center for British Art had a Drupal 7 museum site and a separate collections app. With Fabrique, we replaced them with Drupal on Pantheon: one site for the visit, and a Solr search for the collection.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need the public site and the collection search to feel like one museum? That is the Yale Center for British Art project.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The Yale Center for British Art holds more than 2,000 paintings, 250 sculptures, about 20,000 drawings and watercolors, 40,000 prints, 35,000 rare books and manuscripts, and a reference library of 40,000 volumes. Before 2019 the museum site was Drupal 7 and the collection search was a separate Blacklight application on Rails. Visitors felt the seam. Fabrique led the design. Knectar built the platform. Accessibility had to meet WCAG 2.0 AA and Yale's own checklist.

What we built

Both properties are Drupal on Pantheon, aligned with Drupal 10 and 11. The museum site uses content types for events, exhibitions, pages, people, and stories, with taxonomies for event type, tag, page type, and people. Navigation follows Fabrique's channels: exhibitions and programs, collections, research and learning, a visit, and about. Museum search is Drupal's, weighted by keyword, promotion, and recency. Collection search is a headless front end on Apache Solr, with facets for collection, creator, date, on-site access, image use, and classification. Editorial workflow covers review before publish. Solr integration work was contributed back.

Outcomes

A visitor can plan a visit and search the collection without feeling they have changed websites. The museum can publish an exhibition on a current Drupal, on hosting it does not have to administer by hand.

submenu.label: Fox Chase Cancer Research
submenu.projectTitle: Fox Chase: A cancer center site patients can navigate
submenu.project_haiku: Fox Chase Cancer Center had years of pages and no clear way through them. With Transit Authority Figures, we rebuilt the site in Drupal so patients, researchers, and the marketing team could each find their way.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a hospital site that patients can use and editors can change? We built that for Fox Chase.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

By 2015 the Fox Chase Cancer Center site in Philadelphia had grown without a plan. Patients needed clinical services and a way to ask for an appointment. Researchers needed their programs visible. Marketing needed to tell a story without calling a developer. The center hired Transit Authority Figures for design and information architecture, and Knectar to build it in Drupal.

What we built

Rob and Damia at Transit Authority Figures designed the homepage, the listings, and the inner pages: a hero, generous type, and photography of clinicians and patients. Editors assemble pages from components, including slideshows, quotes, related stories, and lists. Search covers doctors, scientists, clinical trials, and programs, including the Google Search Appliance the center already used. Video, maps, calendars, and forms stay on their outside hosts and embed cleanly. Text can scale to 200 percent, images have alternative text, and the layout holds on a phone.

Outcomes

A patient can find a service. An editor can publish a story inside the design. The site meets the accessibility bar Temple University set for this work.

submenu.label: Kettering University
submenu.projectTitle: Kettering University: Drupal 10 for a co-op university
submenu.project_haiku: Kettering's site had to explain a co-op university, not a typical campus. With Carnegie Higher Ed, we rebuilt it on Drupal 10 in phases the content owners could absorb.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a university rebuild that ships in phases your editors can learn? That is how Kettering went live.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Kettering University teaches through co-op. The public site had to show programs, research, and that model, and it had to do it on a current Drupal with accessible markup. Carnegie Higher Ed led design and strategy. Knectar built it.

What we built

The implementation moved the site to Drupal 10 and replaced leftover paragraphs with a smaller component set. Templates cover programs, co-op, and research, including the university's focus on mobility, energy, manufacturing, and sustainability. Program data, events, news, social posts, and faculty profiles come from the systems that already own them. Carnegie's plan split the work into phases: an approved component inventory, then the global theme, then successive releases with training between them.

Outcomes

Kettering has a Drupal 10 site its content owners were trained on as it shipped, and a component list short enough to maintain.

submenu.label: La Jolla Country Day School
submenu.projectTitle: La Jolla Country Day: A school site in three divisions
submenu.project_haiku: La Jolla Country Day School serves about 1,175 students from age 3 through grade 12. With Verso Design, we built a site organized the way the school is organized: lower, middle, and upper.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a school site that follows the way the school is actually divided? We built that with Verso for La Jolla Country Day.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

La Jolla Country Day School is an independent college-preparatory school of about 1,175 students, from age 3 through grade 12. Families needed a way through three divisions, and through academics, arts, athletics, and admission, without a different logic on every page. Verso Design led the brand and the words. Knectar built the site.

What we built

The information architecture follows the lower, middle, and upper schools. Content types cover academics, arts, athletics, and community service. The site includes an events calendar, a faculty directory, and admission inquiry forms. Verso's visual system and messaging run through the templates. The earlier project record listed the CMS as WordPress. The case study itself describes a Drupal build, and the technology line now matches that account.

Outcomes

A family can start from a division and reach the program, the people, and the inquiry form. The school can edit those pages in the CMS.

submenu.label: Lewis Katz School of Medicine - Temple University
submenu.projectTitle: Lewis Katz School of Medicine: A Drupal site with a faculty directory
submenu.project_haiku: Temple's medical school needed a public site editors could change, and a faculty directory people could search. With Transit Authority Figures, we built both on Drupal.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a school of medicine site with a directory and an approval step before publish? We built that for Lewis Katz.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The Lewis Katz School of Medicine at Temple University had a public site that was hard to edit, visually inconsistent, and short of the university's accessibility standard. Transit Authority Figures, Rob and Damia, led design and information architecture. Knectar built the Drupal site.

What we built

The homepage is a slideshow that can sit as a single slide, plus quick links and a block placer. Inner pages are assembled by editors, who can embed a slideshow in the body with Node Embed. The faculty directory searches by name, alphabet, research center, and basic-science or clinical department, and suggests names as you type. Workbench roles separate the people who draft from the people who publish. Text uses relative sizes and can scale to 200 percent. Images have an alternative-text field.

Outcomes

A prospective student or a colleague can find a program and a person. An editor can build a page. Publishing still passes through someone with permission to publish.

submenu.label: LIM College
submenu.projectTitle: LIM College: A redesign that kept the Drupal content
submenu.project_haiku: LIM College needed a clearer site for the business of fashion, without throwing away the Drupal 9 content it already had. With Carnegie Higher Ed, we reskinned and restructured the site in place.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a redesign that keeps the content you have already paid to create? That is the LIM College project.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

LIM College, in New York, teaches the business of fashion. In 2023 the public site was Drupal 9 and already full of programs, aid, news, and landing pages. Navigation was hard to follow, program pages did not answer a prospective student's questions, and the calls to action were buried. Carnegie Higher Ed led the creative strategy. Knectar implemented it. The constraint was to keep the content and the installation.

What we built

Primary navigation was rewritten: online programs got their own pages, Internships+ became Careers and Internships, and Admissions and Apply stopped competing for the same job. The homepage carries the brand, a program finder, student stories, and requests to get information, visit, or apply. The finder filters by degree, on-campus or online, field, and career. Existing nodes stayed. The look changed around them.

Outcomes

LIM has a current public site and the same body of content. Editors were not asked to start over.

submenu.label: Madison Country Day School
submenu.projectTitle: Madison Country Day: A Drupal site for an IB school
submenu.project_haiku: Madison Country Day School needed pages for an IB curriculum, arts, athletics, and admission that teachers could edit. With Verso Design, we built that on Drupal Paragraphs.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a school site your teachers can build a page in? We did that with Verso for Madison Country Day.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Madison Country Day School is an independent Pre-K through 12 International Baccalaureate school. The public site had to carry a demanding curriculum and still be editable by the people who run the programs. Verso Design led the identity and the message. Knectar built the site.

What we built

Pages are Drupal Paragraphs, so a teacher or an admissions editor can assemble a page for the IB program, the arts, athletics, or a visit. Verso's visual system is in the components, which keeps a new page inside the identity.

Outcomes

The school can publish a program page without a developer, and the page still looks like Madison Country Day.

submenu.label: MIT
submenu.projectTitle: MIT Solve: A Drupal platform for challenges and solvers
submenu.project_haiku: MIT Solve matches people who have a hard problem with people who might work on it. We built the Drupal platform where those challenges, teams, and resources meet.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a site that is a working match between a problem and the people who take it on? MIT Solve is that platform.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

MIT Solve runs open challenges on problems such as climate and learning. The site had to do more than describe the initiative. A challenge, a solver, and a resource had to be findable and connected. The public site is solve.mit.edu.

What we built

The platform is Drupal. Challenges, solver profiles, and the resources attached to them are structured content, so a visitor can move from a problem to the people working on it. Staff publish a new challenge without a new template for every one.

Outcomes

Solve has a site that behaves like the program: a challenge is a record, a team is a record, and the two can be found from each other.

submenu.label: Northeastern Illinois University
submenu.projectTitle: Northeastern Illinois University: A Drupal site for a Chicago campus
submenu.project_haiku: NEIU is one of the most diverse public universities in the Midwest, with more than one Chicago campus. With Carnegie Higher Ed, we built a Drupal site organized around programs, students, and how to get there.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a university site that leads with programs and how to apply? We built NEIU's with Carnegie Higher Ed.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Northeastern Illinois University serves a diverse student body at several Chicago locations. Rankings from the Wall Street Journal, Times Higher Education, and U.S. News have put it at or near the top of Midwest universities for diversity. The site had to make programs and campuses understandable to someone who does not already know the school. Carnegie Higher Ed led the enrollment-focused strategy. Knectar built the Drupal site.

What we built

Program pages carry the academic offering and student stories. An interactive map covers the campuses. The templates follow Carnegie's enrollment patterns: what you can study, who studies it, and how to take the next step.

Outcomes

A prospective student can move from a program to a campus to an inquiry. NEIU staff edit those pages in Drupal.

submenu.label: University of Massachusetts, Amherst
submenu.projectTitle: UMass Amherst HFA: One Drupal pattern for twenty departments
submenu.project_haiku: The College of Humanities and Fine Arts at UMass Amherst has more than twenty departments. With Transit Authority Figures, we built a Drupal distribution so each one could launch on the same design.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need many department sites that still look like one college? UMass HFA is that distribution.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The College of Humanities and Fine Arts at UMass Amherst houses more than twenty departments, programs, and centers. Each needed a site. The college needed them to look related. Transit Authority Figures led the design. Knectar built the Drupal distribution.

What we built

A department starts from the shared design. Content types and taxonomies cover programs, faculty, and events. A Blocks Placer lets an editor position slideshows, accent colors, and the other provided blocks. The design includes a rotating footer background and a moving logo.

Outcomes

A department can launch without a new design. The college keeps one visual system. Editors arrange the blocks they were given.

label: Intranets & Portals
categoryDescription: From robust intranets to dynamic portals, Knectar builds secure, scalable platforms that streamline communication and collaboration for organizations of all sizes.

submenu.label: Massachusetts Municipal Wholesale Electric Company
submenu.projectTitle: MMWEC: A member portal and a rebate application
submenu.project_haiku: Massachusetts municipal utilities needed a private place for reports and a public path for NextZero rebates. We built both on Drupal: a member portal with permissions by town, and the rebate application in front of it.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a portal where each member sees only their own reports? MMWEC is that system, plus the rebate application their customers use.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

MMWEC is the joint-action agency for Massachusetts municipal utilities. It serves member light departments with power supply, finance, and risk management, and it runs NextZero, the efficiency program those utilities offer their customers. Reports were moving by email. Rebates needed a real application, not a PDF on a page.

What we built

The member portal is Drupal. A utility user sees the reports, invoices, budgets, and notes their town is allowed to see. Staff file meeting notes, marketing, and newsletters under the same role rules. NextZero customers start rebate requests for audits, appliances, heat pumps, and the measures their utility has chosen to offer.

Outcomes

A member town opens the portal and finds its own documents. A customer starts a rebate without mailing a form. MMWEC staff control who sees which file.

submenu.label: AB InBev
submenu.projectTitle: AB InBev: A wholesale ordering portal, country by country
submenu.project_haiku: AB InBev needed wholesale buyers to reorder across brands and countries without a different system in each market. We built a Magento portal that deploys per country and talks to the backends they already run.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a B2B store that can be stood up for another country without a new build? That is the portal we shipped for AB InBev.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

AB InBev, one of the world's largest beverage companies, asked for a wholesale ordering portal for Latin America and beyond. Retail and hospitality buyers had to reorder a large catalog, across brands, in more than one language, with permissions that match how a distributor actually works.

What we built

The store is Magento Enterprise, one container stack per country, on AWS. Each country keeps its own catalog, prices, and API rules. Mulesoft carries orders and product data to the country backends. Redis, RDS, a load balancer, and CloudFront keep the storefront available. Buyers get a tiled catalog and filters that work on a phone in a store.

Planning covered a template matrix for how products appear, wireframes with AB InBev's Latin America UX team, and test scripts for deploy, product sync, orders, roles, and language switching.

Outcomes

A buyer in one country reorders in that country's catalog, and the same pattern can be deployed for the next country. The portal is the wholesale counter, not a consumer brand site.

submenu.label: SmartLabs
submenu.projectTitle: SmartLabs: A public site, a member portal, and vivarium tools
submenu.project_haiku: SmartLabs runs turnkey labs in more than one city. With Aaron Taylor-Waldman, we built three connected products on Drupal: the public site, a member portal with single sign-on, and the vivarium compliance tools.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a public site and a private system for the people who use the building? SmartLabs is both, on one platform.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

SmartLabs leases equipped labs, from wet lab to vivarium, in Boston, Cambridge, and San Francisco. As the buildings multiplied, the website, the member tools, and the animal-care paperwork were separate problems. A tenant needed a private workspace. SmartLabs staff needed to see across tenants. Compliance for animal research could not live in email.

What we built

The public site is the marketing front: programs, locations, 360-degree tours, and case material, editable by staff who are not developers. Aaron Taylor-Waldman led the design. The member portal is multi-tenant. Identity runs through the customer's SSO, including Okta, OneLogin, and Azure, with directory data from LDAP. It connects to the systems SmartLabs already uses: BioRAFT for safety, TEEM for rooms, Zendesk for tickets, HubSpot or Salesforce for the customer record, and WiCom for vivarium hardware. Vivarium workflows cover IACUC and IBC forms, badge limits, physical access, and the records an AAALAC review expects.

Outcomes

A prospect can read the offer. A member signs in and reaches their lab's tools. Animal-care compliance has a system of record instead of a shared inbox.

label: Web & iOS Apps
categoryDescription: We design and develop custom web and iOS applications that delight users and drive results. Our apps are crafted for performance, accessibility, and seamless integration.

submenu.label: Carv Resource Management
submenu.projectTitle: Carv: Prototypes that show whether the team can cover the work
submenu.project_haiku: Time trackers record what already happened. Carv asks whether today's people can cover the work that is still in the pipeline. We built two prototypes: a browser simulator and a curved hours allocator.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a planning tool that treats a pipeline as a forecast, not a timesheet? Carv is the prototype we built for that question.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Small and mid-sized teams can tell you what they logged. They cannot tell you whether a late client, a slow hire, or a surprise win will leave a role short in six weeks. Carv started from that question. The stack on this project is Django and Angular, and the two tools below are the working prototypes.

What we built

The pipeline simulator runs in the browser. A project template holds up to five role blocks inside a 26-week window. Planners drag the blocks. Each new deal clones the template. Full-time equivalents become a capacity line at 40 hours each. A feed rate controls how fast new work arrives. Every project sits in a confidence band: 25, 50, 75, or 100 percent, depending on where it is between first conversation and signed work.

A second prototype allocates hours along a curve, so a role can ramp and taper instead of sitting as a flat block on a calendar.

Outcomes

A planner can see a shortage before the week arrives, and can see which assumption, the feed of new work or the confidence of a deal, created it.

submenu.label: Glassica App
submenu.projectTitle: Glassica: Three prototypes of one hexagon puzzle
submenu.project_haiku: Glassica is a puzzle of rotating hexagonal rings and colors that mix when they overlap. We prototyped it as an iOS app, a two-player game in p5.js, and a laser-cut board.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need to find out if a game works before you commit to one platform? Glassica is three prototypes of the same rules.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The idea was a board of concentric hexagonal rings, polyiamond pieces, and colors that mix. It had to work as a solitaire puzzle and as a two-player contest. The way to learn that was to build it more than once.

What we built

The first prototype is an iOS puzzle. Pieces snap to the grid, rings rotate by a drag, and overlapping primary colors mix. A full hexagon of a complementary color clears and scores. The second is a two-player version in p5.js, to test territory rather than a solo clear. The third is a physical board, cut by laser, so the same rotation could be tried with hands.

The technology line on this project is C# and Unity, which is where the native prototype work sat alongside the p5.js and the physical board.

Outcomes

The rules survived contact with a screen and with a table. That is what the prototypes were for.

submenu.label: Music apps
submenu.projectTitle: Music apps: Jazz Hero and two more practice tools
submenu.project_haiku: Jazz Hero writes a practice line over a chord progression you choose. It is one of three browser tools in this set. Django and Angular run Jazz Hero. The others are Strudelizer and Musical Call and Response.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a practice tool that is a real app, with accounts and a saved progression? Jazz Hero is that, and two more sketches sit beside it.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

These are tools for working on music in the browser: pick a harmony, generate a line, hear it, keep it. The one built out furthest is Jazz Hero. Strudelizer and Musical Call and Response are the other two studies in the set.

What we built

Jazz Hero is a Django API and an Angular front end. You choose or write a progression and a key, set density, rests, range, and the kinds of approach tones you want, and the app writes a treble line and a bass line. You can audition it and download MIDI. An account saves progressions. Angular Material supplies the controls. The generator is rule-based, not a model.

The technology line includes Cursor and JavaScript, which is the workshop these browser tools were built in.

Outcomes

A player can generate a line over changes they actually use, listen, and come back to the progression later. The other two apps are in the same family of sketches.

submenu.label: Choosroozy
submenu.projectTitle: Choosroozy: A decision you can drag
submenu.project_haiku: Choosroozy puts two options on a canvas and lets you drag the reasons until the choice is visible. It is a small JavaScript tool for a decision that was previously all in your head.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Want a small interface that makes an abstract choice concrete? Choosroozy is that kind of sketch, built and usable.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Most decisions stay invisible. You hold two options and a pile of reasons, and the loudest reason wins. Choosroozy is a sketch of the other way: put the options on screen and move the reasons by hand.

What we built

Two choices sit on a canvas, "go for a run" against "take a nap," or any pair you type. Each factor is a circle. Drag it left or right to take a side. Drag it up or down to change its weight. Color shows which option the factor supports, and a mixed color shows a factor that pulls both ways.

The sketch is in p5.js and runs in the browser. You can try it from the project link.

Outcomes

The decision is a picture you can edit. That is the whole product, and it is enough to show how a small interface can carry a real task.

submenu.label: Paragraphs Stats Module
submenu.projectTitle: Paragraphs Stats: A Drupal report of which components are used
submenu.project_haiku: Large Drupal sites collect paragraph types nobody can account for. Paragraphs Stats is the contributed module we wrote so an editor can see which components are used, where, and which are idle.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: About to redesign a Drupal site and unsure which components are actually in use? Paragraphs Stats is the report we open first.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Paragraphs lets editors build pages from components. On a long-running site the list of paragraph types passes twenty, and nobody can say which ones are used. Cleaning up means guessing, or writing a one-off query. We needed that answer on our own client sites, so we built it as a module.

What we built

Paragraphs Stats is a contributed Drupal module, at drupal.org/project/ps. It depends on Paragraphs. Once enabled, Reports includes a Paragraphs Stats report, limited to roles you grant. The report shows how often each paragraph type is used and which content types contain it, which is enough to retire an unused component or to see whether a new one was adopted.

Outcomes

A content lead can answer "is this component used?" without a developer and a SQL window. We use it on client sites. Anyone else on Drupal can install it.

label: Informational
categoryDescription: Knectar specializes in creating engaging informational sites that inform, inspire, and connect audiences. We turn complex ideas into clear, accessible digital experiences.

submenu.label: AIER:  American Institute for Economic Research.
submenu.projectTitle: AIER: From Drupal 6 to a site the editors can run
submenu.project_haiku: The oldest economic research institute in the country was still publishing on Drupal 6, with two content types where one would do. We moved AIER to Drupal 7 and a shorter list of types their staff can actually edit.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Sitting on a CMS your editors work around? We rebuilt AIER so the research could be filed once and found.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The American Institute for Economic Research, founded in 1933 in Great Barrington, publishes research, news, and teaching material. The site was Drupal 6. Articles and homepage "buckets" were separate nodes. Staff had a long path to put a paper on the front page, and the archive still had to stay findable.

What we built

The migration landed on Drupal 7 and six content types. Research articles absorbed the old article and bucket split, with "promote to front page," a taxonomy, related articles, and media on the node. News can point at an outside source and record the outbound click. Research keeps a twelve-month display cycle without dropping the document from the archive.

Outcomes

Editors file a paper once. The homepage, the mobile page, and the archive read from that same record.

submenu.label: SMMA Architecture
submenu.projectTitle: SMMA: A WordPress site for an architecture practice
submenu.project_haiku: SMMA needed a site that could show a building as a project, not a thumbnail. With TOKY, we built it on WordPress, with fields the marketing team can fill in and a catalog of the firm's work.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a portfolio site your marketing team can add a project to? SMMA is that site.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

SMMA is an architecture and engineering firm working in education, workplace, healthcare, and life sciences. The site had to present projects with some depth, and the people who win the work had to be able to publish a project without a developer. TOKY led the design, in Figma. Knectar built it.

What we built

The site is WordPress and Elementor, with Advanced Custom Fields for the project record. Blocks cover the pieces TOKY designed: a before-and-after of rendering and photograph, image and story, galleries, accordions, and quotes. HubSpot receives the forms. Gravity Forms handles gated downloads. SmashBalloon brings in Instagram. Tinify compresses images on the way in. Real Media Library keeps the files organized.

Outcomes

SMMA can add a project, a form, and a gallery. The page structure is the one TOKY drew, filled in by the firm.

submenu.label: Monadnock Media
submenu.projectTitle: Monadnock Media: A newsroom site editors can run
submenu.project_haiku: A weekly newspaper in the Monadnock region needed a site its editors could run. We built a Strapi newsroom and, with Aaron Taylor-Waldman, a front end that keeps the reading first.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a content site your staff can publish, with a front end built to a designer's spec? That is the work we did for Monadnock Media.
submenu.pageSummary:
Client background

Monadnock Media publishes the Monadnock Ledger-Transcript, a weekly paper for the Monadnock region of New Hampshire. The site had to do two jobs at once: give editors a place to draft, schedule, and publish, and give readers a paper that still felt like a paper on a phone.

Project goals and challenges

The paper needed a site the newsroom could run without a developer on every story, and a reading experience that could carry a designed front end.

  • Editors needed articles, authors, categories, and media in one system, with drafts and a schedule that matched a weekly. Strapi was the CMS.
  • The front end had to follow Aaron Taylor-Waldman's design and still read clearly on a phone. Knectar built that front end.
  • Motion had to frame a story and then leave it alone. Scroll, parallax, and layered art stayed in scope where the type remained readable and the page stayed fast.
  • Journalists had to file in a system that matched the newsroom. Roles, drafts, and the publishing schedule had to feel like the paper's week.
  • The story had to load quickly and turn up in search. A local paper is opened between other things, often on a phone.

Approach

Strapi as the newsroom

Strapi holds the paper: articles, authors, categories, tags, and media, with the fields and relationships a weekly uses. Editors draft, schedule, and publish there. Roles follow the newsroom. The front end reads the API, so a design change does not require a CMS rebuild, and a CMS change does not require a redesign.

Front end, with the design partner

Knectar built the front end to Aaron Taylor-Waldman's design. Scroll-triggered playback, parallax, and layered sections sit where they frame a story. Svelte runs those interactions so the reading column stays light.

Performance and the reading column

Images and video load as the reader reaches them. The reading column is the page. Motion is additional, and it is kept from delaying the story or breaking the layout on a phone.

Outcomes

The newsroom publishes from Strapi: drafts, a schedule, media, and the roles the staff already had. Readers get the Ledger-Transcript in a layout built with Aaron Taylor-Waldman, including scroll and layered art that leave the article readable. The phone is the same site.

submenu.label: Robert Rauschenberg Foundation
submenu.projectTitle: Robert Rauschenberg Foundation: Drupal 7 to Drupal 10
submenu.project_haiku: The Rauschenberg Foundation's site was Drupal 7, much of it trapped in Views, with the art records living in FileMaker. We moved it to Drupal 10 so editors can build pages, and the archive still imports.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Inheriting a Drupal 7 site that only a developer can edit? The Rauschenberg Foundation was that project.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The Robert Rauschenberg Foundation stewards the artist's work, archive, programs, and residencies. By 2024 the public site was Drupal 7: dozens of content types, pages assembled entirely in Views, more than a thousand artwork records, and a FileMaker database as the source for much of the art and archive. Staff who were not developers could not safely change a page.

What we built

The site is Drupal 10. Simple pages were migrated by hand. Artworks, series, and archive records came across by script. Several near-duplicate "basic page" types collapsed into one. Editors compose the homepage and program pages in Layout Builder. Artwork and archive records import from FileMaker on a schedule through the Feeds FileMaker module: descriptive fields stay with FileMaker, and a few Drupal-only fields stay editable by curators. Search and filtering use Search API and Facets. On View and Public Collections became one map with two kinds of pins. Chronology was slated for an interactive timeline. Exhibition history moved from book pages to ordinary pages.

Outcomes

An editor can change a hero, a news block, or a program tile without editing a View. New artwork reaches the site from FileMaker without a retype. The public can search the art and see where work is on view.

submenu.label: Jack Daniels
submenu.projectTitle: Jack Daniel's: A global Drupal site with Arnold Worldwide
submenu.project_haiku: Jack Daniel's needed one site for a global audience, a mobile screen, and a 150-year-old distillery. Knectar built the Drupal back end. Arnold Worldwide designed and built the front end.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a brand site that can be different in each country and still be one system? We were the Drupal team on Jack Daniel's.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

By 2012 jackdaniels.com had to carry a heritage brand, product detail, distillery visits, recipes, and commerce links, and it had to do that for visitors in different countries on phones as well as desks. Age gates and local rules came with the category. Brown-Forman hired Arnold Worldwide for the experience and Knectar for the Drupal architecture.

What we built

Arnold's front-end team designed and built the interface. Knectar built the Drupal back end that serves localized content, the product and visit information, and the responsive templates. The public site is one system with a version for the visitor's country.

Outcomes

A visitor gets the brand, the product, and the distillery in one place, in a layout that fits the screen they brought, under the rules of the country they are in.

submenu.label: Studio Arts Consortium International (SACI), Florence
submenu.projectTitle: SACI Florence: A Drupal site for an art school abroad
submenu.project_haiku: SACI is an American art school in two Florentine palaces. With Stoltze Design, we rebuilt the Drupal site so a student can find a program and apply without getting lost in the archive.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a school site that can hold years of content and still lead to an application? SACI was that rebuild.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Studio Arts College International was founded in Florence in 1975 by the painter Jules Maidoff. It is a U.S.-accredited art school, the oldest American one in the city, and it holds classes in Palazzo dei Cartelloni and Palazzo Maidoff. Years of program, student, and gallery content had piled up. Prospective students could not reliably find a program or the application. Stoltze Design led the identity. Knectar built the Drupal site.

What we built

The redesign covered information architecture, templates for programs, admissions, student life, events, and galleries, directories, and forms. The existing content was migrated. The sitemap was rebuilt around the questions a student actually has. Stoltze's identity, a logo with traditional proportions and a stronger color, is the visual system on the templates.

Outcomes

A student can move from a program to admissions. Staff edit a large site without the old pile of one-off layouts. The content that was worth keeping came across.

submenu.label: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
submenu.projectTitle: Gardner Museum: Drupal for the collection and the visit
submenu.project_haiku: The Gardner Museum needed a site for the palace, the collection, and the visit, with the object records coming from Embark. With Fabrique, we built that on Drupal 8.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a museum site that can publish an exhibition and stay tied to the collection database? The Gardner Museum is that project.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, opened in 1903, shows a personal collection in a Venetian-style palace in Boston. The site had to cover exhibitions, events, stories, rooms, and more than 2,500 objects, without turning the palace into a database. Object data lives in Embark. Fabrique led the design. Knectar built the site.

What we built

The CMS is Drupal 8. Content types and paragraphs cover exhibitions, events, stories, audio, and rooms. Roles run from contributor to editor to admin. Embark sends object metadata as XML. eMuseum handles the related digital assets. Vocabularies for artist, century, place, and object type stay aligned with the collection system. Audio plays through LibSyn. Search and filters run across the content types. Room views give a visitor a way through the palace, not only through a search box.

Outcomes

Staff can publish an exhibition or a story. An object on the site still comes from the collection system. A visitor can plan a visit or follow a room.

submenu.label: Way Finders
submenu.projectTitle: Way Finders: One Drupal site for three lines of work
submenu.project_haiku: Way Finders, formerly HAP Housing, needed one site for housing help, real estate, and community work, during a rebrand. We built it as one Drupal codebase with four public faces.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Rebranding an organization that does more than one thing? Way Finders needed one site that could show all three.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Way Finders is a NeighborWorks organization in Massachusetts, focused on affordable housing. The rebrand from HAP Housing had to land on the web, and the site had to carry three lines of work: the Housing Center, real estate development, and community engagement. Outside systems already owned pieces of the operation: Newton Software, Eventbrite, Blackbaud eTapestry, and GoSection8.

What we built

One Drupal codebase serves four sections: the main organization, Housing Center, real estate, and community engagement. They share templates and taxonomy and wear different navigation. Content types cover gateway pages, properties with galleries and filters, a staff directory, a resource library, and news. Google Translate covers languages. The outside systems stay where they are and connect at the edges.

Outcomes

A visitor can tell which line of work they need and stay inside one organization. Staff edit all four sections in one CMS. The rebrand has a site that matches it.

label: E-Commerce
categoryDescription: Our e-commerce solutions empower businesses to grow online. From custom storefronts to seamless integrations, we help brands reach new customers and maximize sales.

submenu.label: Chemex Coffee Maker
submenu.projectTitle: Chemex: A Shopify catalog for a brewer people already know
submenu.project_haiku: Chemex has made the same hourglass brewer in Chicopee since the design was patented in 1941. We built the Shopify store that presents that catalog without burying the object.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a store that can carry a catalog and still feel like the product? That is the Chemex shop.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Chemex Corporation manufactures the pour-over brewer Peter Schlumbohm patented in 1941. The glass carafe and bonded filter are still assembled at the factory in Chicopee, Massachusetts. The shop had to present the full range of brewers and filters and keep the object recognizable.

What we built

The site is Shopify. Navigation covers the classic series and the rest of the brewing line. Product pages carry the materials and the use of the brewer. The photography and the type do the explaining. The cart stays out of the way of the product.

Outcomes

A buyer can find the brewer, the filters, and the rest of the line, and the page still reads as Chemex.

submenu.label: Guardair
submenu.projectTitle: Guardair: A Shopify catalog for industrial safety tools
submenu.project_haiku: Guardair has made safety air guns since 1942. We built a Shopify Plus catalog so an industrial buyer can find the right gun, vacuum, or part and the compliance notes that go with it.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need an industrial catalog your buyers can search and your team can update? Guardair is that store.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Guardair invented the safety air gun in Bridgeport in 1942 and later worked with OSHA on a gun that met the new rules. The line now includes pneumatic vacuums, syphon spray guns, and the products that came with Allpax, Nortech, and Air-Spade. Buyers needed a catalog, not a brochure.

What we built

The site is Shopify Plus, built with Tunnel7. Hundreds of SKUs are grouped into air-gun series, vacuum families, including NED and ATEX units, and the rest of the safety line. Product pages carry the specifications a buyer checks before ordering. The team can add a SKU without a deploy.

Outcomes

An industrial buyer can move from a category to a part. Guardair's staff can keep the catalog current.

submenu.label: Pioneer Valley Books
submenu.projectTitle: Pioneer Valley Books: A Shopify store for K–6 literacy
submenu.project_haiku: Pioneer Valley Books sells leveled readers and teaching tools to schools. With Tunnel7, we built a Shopify Plus catalog organized the way a reading teacher shops: by program, level, and classroom use.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a catalog organized the way your buyer already thinks? Pioneer Valley Books is that store.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Michèle Dufresne started Pioneer Valley Books in 1998 because she could not find leveled books she wanted to teach with. The company now sells K–6 reading programs, books, and professional tools to schools. A teacher or a specialist has to find a program, see what it teaches, and order the set.

What we built

The site is Shopify Plus, with Tunnel7. The catalog is grouped by reading programs, books and libraries, phonics, and tools such as the digital reader, assessments, and decodable books. A program page states the objective, the scope and sequence, and the bundles. Schools can move from a literacy goal to a cart.

Outcomes

An educator can find the program and the materials that go with it. Pioneer Valley can merchandise a bundle without a custom page for every SKU.

submenu.label: Sleep Studio
submenu.projectTitle: Sleep Studio: A Magento store for a mattress line
submenu.project_haiku: Sleep Studio sells gel and copper-infused foam, with a 100-night trial. We built the Magento store so a buyer can compare a topper, a pillow, and a bundle and check out.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a product catalog that explains a physical product and then gets out of the way of the cart? Sleep Studio is that shop.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Sleep Studio sells the SleepJoy line: gel memory foam, copper-infused foam, toppers, and pillows, made in the U.S. The brand offers a 100-night trial and free shipping. The site had to explain the materials and make the purchase obvious.

What we built

The store is Magento. Categories cover toppers, pillows, and seasonal groups such as back-to-college. Landing pages use the product photography and the material claims. A buyer can move from a category to a product to checkout without a second explanation of the same foam.

Outcomes

The catalog matches the line. The trial and the materials are on the page where the decision happens.

submenu.label: Sparx Hockey
submenu.projectTitle: Sparx Hockey: A Shopify store for a skate sharpener
submenu.project_haiku: Sparx sells an at-home skate sharpener to players, rinks, and pro shops. With Magnifico Design, we built the Shopify store for the machine, the rings, the parts, and the instructions.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Selling a product people also have to learn how to use? Sparx is a store and a manual in one site.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Sparx Hockey, in Acton, Massachusetts, makes an automated skate sharpener for hockey, figure skating, and sled hockey. Buyers are families, teams, rinks, and shops. The site had to sell the machine and explain the grinding rings, the service plan, and the edge sensor that goes with it. The company is the NHL's preferred at-home sharpener. Magnifico Design led the design. Knectar built the store.

What we built

The site is Shopify. Navigation covers sharpeners, grinding rings, accessories, bundles, service plans, parts, and the Sparx BEAM edge monitor. Bundles pair a sharpener with rings. Product and help content sit on the same site, so a buyer can read how a ring works before adding it.

Outcomes

A player can buy the sharpener and the right ring. A rink can find parts and a service plan. Sparx can merchandise a bundle without a separate campaign site.

submenu.label: Trillium Brewing
submenu.projectTitle: Trillium Brewing: A Shopify store for more than one taproom
submenu.project_haiku: Trillium grew from a Fort Point taproom in 2013 to several locations and a wide list of beers. We built the Shopify store that sells the beer and points people at the right room.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Selling from more than one location, with more than one way to order? Trillium's store had to do that.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

JC and Esther Tetreault opened Trillium in Fort Point in 2013. The company grew to hundreds of people, more taprooms, a production brewery in Canton, and a farm in North Stonington. The site had to sell beer, explain the locations, and carry more than one way to order.

What we built

The store is Shopify. Product pages cover the range, from New England IPAs to mixed-fermentation beers and the other drinks. Location content covers Fort Point, Fenway, the Greenway beer garden, Canton, and the farm. Ordering is part of the same site as the story of the beer.

Outcomes

A customer can find a beer and a taproom. Trillium can add a release without a separate microsite for every one.

submenu.label: Lanshin
submenu.projectTitle: Lanshin: A Shopify store the staff can run
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Sandra Chiu's Lanshin practice sells tools, skincare, body care, internal formulas, courses, and treatments. The shop had to hold that range and still be editable by people who are not developers.

What we built

The site is Shopify. Staff edit pages, the homepage, products, and menus in the admin. Categories cover tools, skin, body, eyes, scalp and hair, internal wellness, sets, and the usual merchandising groups: featured, new, best sellers. A product page carries the full description, how to use it, and the related details a buyer needs before ordering. The layout is built for a phone.

Outcomes

Lanshin's team can publish a product, a course, and a homepage change. The catalog is browsable by what the product is for.
submenu.project_haiku: Lanshin needed one shop for Chinese medicine tools, skincare, courses, and treatments. We built it on Shopify so the team can change products and pages without a developer.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a shop your staff can update, with a catalog that is more than one kind of product? Lanshin is that store.

label: Music & Art
categoryDescription: We celebrate creativity through digital projects in music and art. Discover how Knectar brings artistic visions to life with technology.

submenu.label: P5 Projects
submenu.projectTitle: p5.js sketches: Four studies in generative drawing
submenu.project_haiku: These four sketches are drawings made of rules: perspective, curves, noise, and interpolation. They are studies in p5.js, written to see what the rule looks like when it runs.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Want to see how a drawing behaves when the rule is the author? These sketches are that work, and the code is the point.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Each sketch is a small question about motion or space, answered with p5.js. The set uses vectors, Bézier curves, Perlin noise, linear interpolation, and perspective. They are studies, not client work.

What we built

Perspective Trace draws hundreds of translucent rectangles from a moving vanishing point, like panes of glass receding. The other sketches in the set use the same habit: set the rule, run it, and keep the version that teaches something about the geometry.

Outcomes

The sketches are the portfolio of that practice. A visitor can see the rule and the picture it makes.

submenu.label: Pen plotting works
submenu.projectTitle: Pen plotting: From a p5.js sketch to an AxiDraw drawing
submenu.project_haiku: A generative sketch of Bézier curves becomes a drawing when a pen plotter can follow it. This piece is that path: p5.js, Inkscape, G-code, and an AxiDraw v3.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Need a generative file that a pen can actually draw? This is the pipeline from the sketch to the plotter.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

A p5.js sketch can fill a screen with curves. A plotter needs vectors, an order of strokes, and a machine that will follow them. The project was to take one Bézier sketch all the way to paper.

What we built

The sketch builds two closed shapes from anchors on a grid. Control points are random, then snapped to the same grid. The design is exported as vectors, edited in Inkscape, converted to G-code, previewed, and drawn on an AxiDraw v3.

Outcomes

The drawing on paper is the same geometry as the sketch, minus everything a pen cannot do. That constraint is the work.

submenu.label: Sculpture works
submenu.projectTitle: Sculpture: Experiments in Material and Flow
submenu.project_haiku: Experiments in Material and Flow is a set of small sculptures about material, fastening, and the forces that shape rock and fluid. They are wall pieces, cut and assembled by hand and by machine.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Looking for fabrication that starts from a material, not a template? These sculptures are that practice.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

Chris Amato's exhibition Experiments in Material and Flow gathers fifteen to twenty small sculptures. Each one is a test of contrast: stone and plaster, a fastener, a curve that comes from flow or from a cut. The pieces range from the size of a baseball to the size of a small dog, and they hang on the wall so you can get close.

What we built

Forms are carved and cast, then joined. CNC and ordinary shop tools both show up, depending on the piece. The technology line is those tools. The subject of the work is the joint and the material, not the machine.

Outcomes

The exhibition is a body of objects. It is also a record of how we move between a digital model and a finished thing.

submenu.label: Thing Y
submenu.projectTitle: Thing Y: A pocket toy, from a file to a sold-out pilot
submenu.project_haiku: Thing Y is a pocket-sized toy about geometry you can hold. Chris Amato designed it in Rhino, had it laser-cut, and sold through a pilot run at A2Z Science and Learning Store in Northampton in 2021.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Have an object that should exist in someone's hand, not only on a screen? Thing Y went from a file to a counter.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The toy had to be small, pleasant to handle, and about geometry rather than a character. It also had to be makeable in a short run, with digital fabrication, and testable with real buyers.

What we built

The form was modeled in Rhino and produced by laser cutting. In 2021 the pilot sat on the counter at A2Z Science and Learning Store in Northampton, Massachusetts. The run sold out.

Outcomes

Thing Y proved a loop we use elsewhere: model, cut, put it in front of a buyer, learn from what leaves the store.

submenu.label: Vases
submenu.projectTitle: Vases: Test Tube Babies, a series of bud vases
submenu.project_haiku: Test Tube Babies is a series of bud vases. A glass tube holds the flower. Hardwood, aluminum, Corian, and colored plastic hold the tube. They are small objects, built as both vases and sculptures.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Interested in objects that are useful and still made one at a time? These vases are that work.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The series needed a flower holder that was also a study of materials. The flower's job is done by a test tube. Everything else is the composition around it.

What we built

Each vase combines hardwood, aluminum sheet, Corian, colored plastic, or plexiglass, joined so the tube sits plumb and the object stands. Warm materials sit next to cool ones on purpose. They are made with ordinary shop tools, which is what the technology line records.

Outcomes

The vases hold flowers. They also hold up as small sculptures. The series is a material study that happens to be useful.

submenu.label: Dog Door
submenu.projectTitle: Dog Door: A door sized for one dog
submenu.project_haiku: Commercial pet doors were the wrong size, the wrong look, or the wrong price. This one was drawn for a specific dog and a specific wall, then cut on a CNC and finished by hand.
submenu.project_footer_CTA: Have a physical problem that the catalog version does not fit? This door is the kind of custom piece we design and build.
submenu.pageSummary:
The job

The dog needed a way through the door. The doors for sale did not fit the opening, the animal, or the house. The project was to design one that did, and to build it so it would last.

What we built

The door was modeled to the opening and the dog, cut with a CNC, and finished with ordinary woodworking tools. The fit, the swing, and the trim were part of the design, not a kit to be disguised later.

Outcomes

The dog uses the door. The wall still looks like the wall. It is a small piece of work, and it shows the same path we use on larger fabrication: measure, draw, cut, finish.
